## 6. An explicit reason readout and purity control are insufficient

Consider the rational faithful states
\[
\rho_n
=
\frac{I-(1-2^{-n})|0^n\rangle\langle0^n|}
{2^n-1+2^{-n}},
\qquad n=L^2.
\]
They satisfy
\[
\|\rho_n-I/2^n\|_1=O(2^{-n}).
\]
For every \(m\)-site marginal,
\[
2^m\operatorname{Tr}\rho_{n,A}^{\,2}-1
=
\frac{(1-2^{-n})^2(2^m-1)}
{(2^n-1+2^{-n})^2}
=
O(2^{-n}).
\]
Nevertheless,
\[
-\log\rho_n
\equiv n\log2\,|0^n\rangle\langle0^n|
\pmod{\mathbb RI}.
\]

For a site \(i\), define
\[
\Delta_i A=A-X_iAX_i.
\]
For distinct, widely separated \(i,j\),
\[
\|\Delta_i\Delta_j(-\log\rho_n)\|_\infty=n\log2.
\]
Any interaction decomposition satisfying your requested bound would imply
\[
\|\Delta_i\Delta_jK\|_\infty
\le
4\sum_{X\ni i,j}\|K_X\|
\le
4C\eta e^{-\mu\,\operatorname{dist}(i,j)}.
\]
These are incompatible as the lattice grows.

This proves that even exponentially accurate control of **all bounded readouts**, together with small marginal collision entropies, does not imply the desired logarithmic locality.

**It is not a counterexample to your model.** In fact, this particular family cannot be stationary at fixed weak \(\eta\). Native reset inflow at its depleted eigenvector would require
\[
\eta\ge\frac{2^n-1}{2d\,2^k}.
\]
That calculation is included in the report precisely to prevent mistaking a logical separation for a model-preserving negative result.

## 7. The cited sources leave the necessary all-order step open

The requested Arad–Firanko–Gurevich paper has the scope stated in your prompt:

- Theorem 3.1 proves geometric support of the Gibbs coefficients for its discrete weak-interaction model.
- Corollary 3.2 assumes an exponential coefficient-norm bound.
- Theorem 3.3 controls coefficients of an observable expansion.
- Section 6 expressly leaves the Gibbs coefficient-norm bound unproved.

Those results cannot be promoted to the present continuous-time, arbitrary-\(g\), uniform operator-logarithm theorem. [arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2408.08672v2?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

A related primary paper, Bluhm–Capel–Pérez-Hernández, reports a gap in an earlier noncommuting effective-Hamiltonian cluster proof. Its own polymer-log theorem requires activities in a **commutative Banach algebra**, and it explicitly invokes that condition when obtaining logarithmic effective interactions.
